questions.question: Who raised the Indian National Army (INA), to free India from British control?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohan Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Azad Hind Fauj or the India National Army (INA) was first established by Mohan Singh in 1942**.

 
 
• It was revived by Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose on October 21, 1943, during the Second World War to secure India’s complete independence from British Raj.
 
• On this day, India’s first independent provisional government named Azad Hind Government was announced.
 
• This was followed by a conference in Bangkok (June 1942), where Rashbehari Bose was elected president of the league and a decision was taken to raise the Indian National Army.
 
• **Captain Mohan Singh was appointed the commander of the INA**, which had about 40,000 Indian soldiers
 
• This conference invited Bose to lead the movement.
 
 
• Earlier, Bose had escaped from India in 1941 to Berlin.
 
• In June 1943 he came to Tokyo and then India joined the INA in Singapore.
 
 
 
• **Rashbehari Bose handed over the leadership to Subhas Bose, and an Azad Hind Sarkar was formed**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhagat Singh** was a revolutionary leader who was executed by the British. 

 
 
• In 1926, he founded the **Naujawan Bharat Sabha**.
 
• In 1928, he established the** Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)** along with Sukhdev, Chandrashekhar Azad, and others.
 
• In April 1926, Bhagat Singh established contact with Sohan Singh Josh and through him the 'Kirti Kisan Party' which brought out the monthly magazine Kirti in Punjabi.
 
• In 1927, he was first arrested on charges of association with the Kakori Case accused for an article written under the pseudonym Vidrohi (Rebel).
 
• Bhagat Singh was re-arrested for the murder of J.P. Saunders and bomb manufacturing in the Lahore Conspiracy case.
 
 
• He was found guilty in this case and was hanged on 23rd March 1931 in Lahore along with Sukhdev and Rajguru.
 
 
 
• **Every year, March 23 is observed as Martyrs’ Day as a tribute to freedom fighters Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru.**

questions.question: What is the 'quorum' required in the State Legislature to hold a meeting?

options.text: Thirty members or one tenth of total membership, whichever is less
One-half of the total membership of the House
One-fourth of the total membership of the House
Ten members or one tenth of the total members of the House, whichever is greater

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The **Quorum **refers to the **number of members that must be present for a house meeting to take place.**
 
• As per** Article 189(3)** of the Indian Constitution, until the Legislature of the State by law otherwise provides, the quorum to constitute a meeting of a House of the Legislature of a State **shall be ten members or one-tenth of the total number of members of the House, whichever is greater.**
 
• For both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, the Constitution established a quorum of **one-tenth of the total membership**.
 
• Thus, at least **55 **members must be present to hold a **Lok Sabha session**, while at least **25 **members must be present to conduct a **Rajya Sabha sitting**.

questions.question: Which part of human brain is responsible for walking in straight line?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The part of the human brain** that is primarily responsible for walking in a **straight line is the cerebellum.**
 
• **The cerebellum is located at the back of the brain, underneath the cerebrum.**
 
• It plays a **crucial role** in coordinating voluntary **movements, including maintaining balance and coordination during walking.**
 
• While other parts of the brain, such as the **motor cortex in the cerebrum**, also contribute to the control of walking, the cerebellum is particularly involved in fine-tuning movements and ensuring smooth, coordinated motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Medulla:** The medulla, also known as the medulla oblongata, is a part of the brainstem located between the pons and the spinal cord.

 
 
• It plays a vital role in controlling several involuntary functions of the body, including breathing, heart rate, blood pressure, and digestion.
 
 
 
• **Cerebrum: **The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain and is divided into two hemispheres.
 
 
• It is responsible for many complex functions, including conscious thought, reasoning, sensory processing, motor control, language, and memory.
 
• The cerebrum is involved in higher cognitive functions and is associated with the conscious perception of walking.
 
 
 
• **Pons:** The pons is a region of the brainstem located above the medulla and below the midbrain. It acts as a bridge connecting different parts of the brain.
 
 
• The pons plays a role in relaying signals between the cerebrum and the cerebellum, as well as regulating sleep, breathing, swallowing, and facial movements.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT form an essential part of the process of photosynthesis?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Photosynthesis:**

 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants and certain other organisms transform light energy into chemical energy.
 
• During photosynthesis in green plants, light energy is captured and used to convert water, carbon dioxide, and minerals into oxygen and energy-rich organic compounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d84acb97efc4a43562014b7ba2d9bc8b57e9a1fdf156d01ebb54d566312556d0.png] 

 
• There are two types of photosynthetic processes: oxygenic photosynthesis and anoxygenic photosynthesis. 
 
• Oxygenic photosynthesis functions as a counterbalance to respiration by taking in the carbon dioxide produced by all breathing organisms and reintroducing oxygen to the atmosphere.
 
• Oxygenic photosynthesis is written as follows: 
 
• 6CO₂ + 12H₂O + Light Energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ + 6H₂O
 
• During oxygenic photosynthesis, light energy transfers electrons from water (H2O) to carbon dioxide (CO2), to produce carbohydrates.
 
• In this transfer, the CO2 is "reduced," or receives electrons, and the water becomes "oxidized," or loses electrons.
 
• Ultimately, oxygen is produced along with carbohydrates.

**Therefore it is clear that Nitrogen does NOT form an essential part of the process of photosynthesis.**

questions.question: Jute grows well on which type of soil?
questions.solution:
__
 
• Soils are complex mixtures of minerals, water, air, organic matter, and countless organisms that are the decaying remains of once-living things.
 
• Soils are formed as a result of weathering of rocks.
 
• Different regions of India have different types of soils.
 
• Each soil has a unique property and characteristics and suitable for particular crop production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

**Jute**:

__
 
• Jute crop requires a hot and humid climate with temperatures between 24 degrees Celsius and 38 degrees Celsius.
 
• **Alluvial sandy loam, clay loamy soils are best suited for jute production.**
 
• Jute is one of the natural fibre crops grown in India.
 
• The cultivation of jute in India is mainly confined to the eastern region of the country.
 
• The jute crop in India is grown in nearly 83 districts of seven states – West Bengal, Assam, Orissa, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Tripura, and Meghalaya. 

**Thus, Jute grows well on Alluvial soil. **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
 

 Types Of Soil
 Characteristics
 
 

 
 
Alluvial soil

 

 
 
 
 
 
 
• Alluvial soil contains silt, sand, clay, and gravel as well as humus, lime, and organic matter. 
 
• It is usually most extensive in the lower part of a river's course, forming floodplains and deltas, but they may form at any point where the river overflows.
 
• Major characteristics of alluvial soil are it is made by the deposition of the river load as it flows from its upper to its lower.
 
• On the basis of its ages alluvial soil is divided into Bhangar (Old alluvium) and Khadar (New alluvium). 
 
• It is porous as well as light, so it is easily tillable.
 
• They are generally rich in potash but poor in phosphorous. 
 
• Alluvial soil is widespread in northern plains and river valleys.
 
• Wheat, rice, maize, sugarcane, pulses, oilseed are mainly cultivated in alluvial soil.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Yellow soil

 

 
 
 
 
 
 
• It develops on **crystalline igneous rocks in areas of low rainfall.**
 
• Especially in** Eastern and Southern Deccan.**
 
• It is** reddish-yellow** in colour.
 
• Red colour due to wide diffusion of iron in crystalline and metamorphic rocks.
 
• Yellow colour when it is in hydrated form.
 
• These soils are fine-grained and fertile.
 
• It is poor in nitrogen, phosphorus and humus.
 
• It is suitable for the cultivation of **rice, wheat, sugarcane, maize/corn, groundnut, ragi (finger millet) and potato, oilseeds, pulses, millets, and fruits.**
 
 
 
 

 
 
Black soil

 
 
 
 
• It has a pH of 6.8.
 
• The parent material for most of the black soil is the volcanic rocks that were formed in the Deccan Plateau.
 
• Black soil covers most of the Deccan Plateau.
 
• This includes parts of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and some parts of Tamil Nadu. 
 
• These soils are also known as the ‘Regur Soil’ or the ‘Black Cotton Soil’.
 
• The colour of the soil ranges from deep black to grey.
 
• The black soils are generally clayey, deep and impermeable.
 
• They swell and become sticky when wet and shrink when dried.
 
• So, during the dry season, this soil develops wide cracks.
 
• They retain moisture for a very long time which helps crops to sustain even during the dry season.
 
• Chemically, the black soils are rich in lime, iron, magnesia and alumina.
 
• But they lack phosphorous, nitrogen and organic matter.
 
 
 
 

 Red soil
 
 
 
• The pH of red soil is more than 5.
 
• Red soil area extends into and includes the greater part of Jharkhand and West Bengal.
 
• Red soils have originated from weathering of the ancient crystalline, and metamorphic rocks.
 
• These are porous, friable and neutral to acidic in nature.
 
• These soils are poor in nitrogen, phosphate, lime and humus. 
 
• Suitable for the cultivation of ragi, groundnut, millet, potato, tobacco, paddy, wheat, and sugarcane.

• It is a chemical reaction in which an acid and base react together to form salt and water as products.

• Decomposition reaction__: The opposite of a combination reaction, a complex molecule breaks down to make simpler ones. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: AB → A + B.

• __Combination reaction__: It is a reaction where two or more elements or compounds combine to form a single compound. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: X + Y → XY.
 
• __Combustion reaction__: Oxygen combines with a compound to form carbon dioxide and water. These reactions are exothermic, meaning they give off heat. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: A + O2 → H2O + CO2.

questions.question: Which of the following laws works in constant pressure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Charle’s law.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Charle’s law**

 
 
• ​**Charles's law **states that the **volume of an ideal gas is directly proportional to the absolute temperature at constant pressure**. 
 
• When the** pressure** that is applied to a sample of a **dry gas** is maintained at the same level, the law also states that the **Kelvin temperature** and the volume will be directly proportional.
 
• **Jacques Charles**, a French physicist, drafted this law in **1780**. His unpublished work provided a comprehensive description of this law.
 
• The **ideal gas** law is a special case of Charle's law.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Boyle’s law**

 
 
• ​Boyle's law is a gas law that says that a gas's pressure is** inversely proportional **to its volume when it has a given mass and is kept at a constant temperature.
 
 
 
• **Thomson’s law**
 
 
• ​Along the length of a material rod whose ends are at different temperatures, **heat power (Qτ) is absorbed or evolved.**
 
• The temperature gradient along the **rod** and the **current flow** were found to be inversely correlated with this heat.
 
 
 
• **Graham’s law**
 
 
• ​A gas's rate of** diffusion or effusion** is** inversely proportional** to the square root of its **molecular weight,** according to Graham's law.
